clue.text: Freely take grub round Canberra at first — in this?

definitions.text: Freely take grub round Canberra at first — in this?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the opening letter of the Australian capital
taken freely, the letters of 'take grub' are rearranged at will
only the first letter of Canberra is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone helping themselves to food near the Australian capital, asking what they carry it in.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle TAKE GRUB and put C, the start of Canberra, inside. The whole clue is the definition: an Australian bag for carrying food, the 'grub' taken freely.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian bushman's sack for carrying provisions is the very thing the clue's grub would go into.

clue.text: Dump outside entrances to urban lorry plant

indicators.note: the word for dump goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump

indicators.note: the entrances are the first letters of urban and lorry

explanation.surface: A rubbish site placed around the gates where city lorries come in.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-flowering bulb with cup-shaped blooms, an example of a garden plant.

clue.text: Time to enter new career as supplier of food

indicators.note: the time letter goes into the rearranged word
a new version of career is a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone changes job late in life and becomes a food supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CAREER and 'to enter' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who provides meals for events is a provider of food by trade.

clue.text: Pilot gets one in a spin, making us flap

indicators.note: letters sent into a spin are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An aircraft pilot with a passenger goes into a spin, which makes us panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a spin' rearranges PILOT GETS plus I. 'us flap' means a flap inside us, not panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap of cartilage in the throat that closes the windpipe when swallowing is a flap within the human body.

clue.text: Game sheltering in scrub in gorge

indicators.note: the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some quarry takes cover in bushes down a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like hunted animals; it is a numbers game, sitting in scruB IN GOrge.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbers-calling hall pastime with cards ticked off is one kind of game.

clue.text: Young chap: good person enthralled by dead PM once

indicators.note: held captive inside the word for dead

parts.note: gone is a euphemism for dead
a lad is a young chap
ST, saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A youngster and a worthy man are captivated by a former prime minister long dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead' gives GONE as a euphemism, and 'good person' is the crossword saint, ST; 'enthralled by' holds them captive.
explanation.definitionFit: William Ewart Gladstone served four terms as British prime minister in the 1800s.

clue.text: Record book

definitions.meaning: an LP or other collection of tracks issued together
a volume for keeping photos or stamps

explanation.definitionFit: Both a long-playing disc and a blank volume for photographs or stamps go by this name.

clue.text: Old Asian maid a poor actor sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word up reads it from the bottom

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts

explanation.surface: A servant from the East mocked an incompetent performer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'sent up' means read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In parts of the old British East, a nursemaid or female servant was known by this word.

clue.text: Air passages booked originally by male Greek character

indicators.note: only the first letter of booked is used

parts.note: Ron is a man's name
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A flight reserved first of all by a Greek man.
explanation.definitionFit: The two main branches of the windpipe carrying air into the lungs are the airways meant.

clue.text: Irish county chap accepting lieutenant for civic office

parts.note: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: the man's name takes the abbreviation into itself

parts.note: Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man from western Ireland takes on an army officer to run for local office.
explanation.definitionFit: The post or term of a town's elected chief magistrate is a civic office.

clue.text: Verse in ancient language inspiring a native of Riga?

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the result takes in the letter A
the verse letter goes into the ancient language

parts.note: Latin is the ancient language of Rome

explanation.surface: Poetry in a dead tongue inspires someone from a Baltic capital.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes into LATIN to make LATVIN, which then breathes in A. The question mark marks a definition by example: Riga is the capital of one Baltic state.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital of the Baltic republic, so someone born there is one of its citizens.

clue.text: Admission of right-winger relating to sexual desire?

parts.note: an admission such as 'I am a ...' supplies the words am a
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A confession by a conservative turns out to be about lust.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the right-winger's confession 'I am a Tory' without the I. The question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things concerning love or erotic longing.

clue.text: Left French department carrying note for Irish town

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
la is a note of the sol-fa scale
the Oise is a department north of Paris

explanation.surface: A departing French official takes a memo to a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' here means taking along beside it: the note sits next to the department rather than inside it. PORT is the nautical word for left.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the county town of County Laois in the Irish midlands.

clue.text: Evidence of injury and endless panic

indicators.note: the word for panic loses its final letter

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic

explanation.surface: Signs of an injury and fear that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left on skin after a wound heals shows the body was once hurt.

clue.text: Component French artist briefly noted initially in food allowance

indicators.note: the painter's name is cut short by one letter

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter

indicators.note: that letter goes into the word for food allowance

parts.note: a diet is a prescribed allowance of food

indicators.note: only the first letter of noted is taken

explanation.surface: A French painter, it is noted, was on a restricted diet.
explanation.walkthrough: INGRES loses its last letter to give INGRE, and N goes into DIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Each item that goes into a recipe or mixture is one of its constituent parts.

clue.text: Weight of ice beginning to accumulate in farm vehicle

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the farm vehicle

parts.note: a cart is a farm wagon

indicators.note: the beginning of accumulate is its first letter

explanation.surface: Ice builds up in a farm wagon, weighing it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' is slang for diamonds, not frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Gems such as diamonds, called ice in slang, are weighed in this unit of 200 milligrams.

clue.text: Vehicle chosen by male member of religious order

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the elite are the chosen few

explanation.surface: A car picked out by a man who belongs to a monastic order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts the male letter beside the word for chosen, before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar or nun of the order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel belongs to a Catholic religious order.

clue.text: Wader shortly to appear around quiet headland

indicators.note: the word for shortly goes around the quiet letter

parts.note: soon means shortly
p, piano, is quiet in music
a bill is a narrow promontory, as in Portland Bill

explanation.surface: Someone in waders will soon turn up near a silent cape.
explanation.walkthrough: Portland Bill is a headland on the English south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird with a flat, broad-tipped beak is a wader of shallow waters.

clue.text: Way proficiency produces steadiness

parts.note: St, street, is a way
ability is skill or proficiency

explanation.surface: Mastering a method gives a steady hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness and freedom from wobbling or change is a synonym of steadiness.

clue.text: Send down girl who's out of practice for speaking?

indicators.note: the phrase is said out loud to give the answer's sound

parts.note: a girl out of practice is rusty, and Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who has lost her touch is expelled for her talk.
explanation.walkthrough: At British universities to be sent down is to be expelled or suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspending a student from a university for a time is the formal sense of this verb.

clue.text: Agitator possibly reading scripture in prison

indicators.note: the reading and scripture letters are put inside the slang word for jail

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs
RE, religious education, is scripture as a school subject

explanation.surface: A troublemaker perhaps studies the Bible while behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals that the definition is by example; reading is one of the three Rs and RE is religious education in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately stirs up trouble or discontent is an agitator.

clue.text: Stony, and lacking 15 dn

definitions.meaning: full of stones, as rough ground is
15 down is steadiness, so lacking it means shaky

explanation.definitionFit: Ground strewn with boulders is stony, and an unsteady, wobbly situation is shaky too.

clue.text: Bone constituent of Scotsman, say, touring Channel Islands

indicators.note: the man's name goes round the abbreviation, as a tourist goes round islands

parts.note: Calum is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot tours Jersey and Guernsey, built of stern stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief mineral element in bones and teeth is this metallic element.

clue.text: Lamb casserole at last, one served in US city?

indicators.note: only the final letter of casserole is taken
the numeral is placed inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lamb stew is finally served to a diner in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is not meat but the essayist Charles Lamb, who wrote as this pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb signed his Essays of the 1820s with this pseudonym.

clue.text: Dramatist quietly crossing river, and later wooded hollow

indicators.note: afterwards the same word also goes round the hollow, further along
the word for quietly is laid across, around, the river letter

parts.note: piano is the musical term for quietly
a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: A playwright quietly crosses a stream and later a wooded valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and later' says the word for quietly also crosses a second piece, further along, after it has taken in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello, Italian author of Six Characters in Search of an Author, was a Nobel-winning playwright.

clue.text: A variable investigator, one of Mexican Indian extraction

parts.note: z is a variable in algebra
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A changeable detective is of Mexican Indian descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the people whose empire ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Algerian port accommodating golf magazine

indicators.note: the port takes the letter in, giving it room

parts.note: Oran is a port city in Algeria
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A North African harbour city houses a golfing periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A publication speaking for a group or party, a house journal, is a magazine of that sort.

clue.text: About end of April money finally comes to bank

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the end of the word April is its closing letter
only the closing letter of money is wanted

explanation.surface: Late in April, money eventually reaches the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' and 'finally' both take a last letter, of April and of money. 'bank' is a verb, as in bank on someone, not a place for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To count on or depend on someone is to put trust in them.

clue.text: Jew, possibly, lives with artist and priest

parts.note: is means lives or exists
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Jewish man perhaps shares his home with a painter and a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Jewish state is likely, though not necessarily, Jewish, hence the 'possibly'.

clue.text: Pouring drink, reportedly, requiring Chinese porcelain

indicators.note: only its spoken sound is wanted

parts.note: tea is a drink
Ming ware is porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: Serving a drink, it is said, calls for fine Chinese china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pouring' looks like serving tea; it means raining heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that is coming down in torrents is said to be bucketing or pouring down.

clue.text: Almost decapitated sooner than expected

indicators.note: the word loses its head, the first letter

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: Someone was nearly beheaded ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving before the expected time is being ahead of schedule.

clue.text: Sailor sporting many hats around Cowes initially

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the initial
sporting suggests playful, so the letters of many hats are rearranged
only the first letter of Cowes is used

explanation.surface: A seafarer wears plenty of hats around the yachting town of Cowes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes, on the Isle of Wight, is home to the famous Cowes Week regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sails pleasure boats is a sailor.
